resources.string: This app is part of an MSc research project studying mobile network quality of experience. Running quietly in the background, it records network signal metrics (like signal strength and quality), approximate location, and which app is in the foreground - only to tag *when* and *under what conditions* a measurement was taken.\n\nIt never reads message content, browsing history, or anything you type. Over the next few screens we\'ll ask for the permissions the app needs to do this reliably, and explain exactly why each one is needed before asking.

ABOUT THIS STUDY

QoESense is part of an MSc research project studying how network signal conditions affect real-world app experience, so that quality of experience can eventually be predicted directly from network data. Participation is completely voluntary: you can stop at any time by disabling collection in the app or uninstalling it, with no consequences.

WHAT WE COLLECT

- Network signal metrics: signal strength and quality (RSRP, RSRQ, SINR), timing advance, network type LTE, a one-way hashed cell tower identifier (not the real ID), and, on some devices, additional channel details.
- Connection info: Wi-Fi vs. cellular, roaming status, an estimate of throughput and latency.
- Approximate location, sampled alongside each network reading, to map coverage along your usual routes.
- Which app is in the foreground, checked periodically - used only to detect whether a social-media app or a video call is active, so we can tag the network conditions during that kind of use. We never see what you typed, sent, or viewed inside any app.
- Your device model, Android version, and the app's own version number.
- Your occasional 1-5 star ratings of network quality, when you respond to a prompt.

WHAT WE NEVER COLLECT

Message content, call content, browsing history, photos, contacts, keystrokes, or anything typed into any app - this app has no access to and does not request any of that.

HOW YOUR DATA IS IDENTIFIED

You are never asked for your name, phone number, or email. Each install gets a random anonymous ID generated by the app, and all your data is tied only to that ID - not to you personally. We have no way to look up who a given ID belongs to from the data alone. Your anonymous ID is shown on the app's Status screen if you ever need to reference it.

WHERE YOUR DATA GOES AND HOW IT'S PROTECTED

Data is uploaded only over Wi-Fi (never using your mobile data), encrypted in transit, and stored on Google Firebase/Cloud infrastructure with access restricted to the research team. Raw signal data is queued locally on your device and only deleted once a successful upload is confirmed.

HOW YOUR DATA IS USED

Your data will be used to build and evaluate multiple deep learning models for predicting network quality of experience, as part of an MSc research project. Aggregated or de-identified results may be published in academic work; individual raw data will not be shared publicly or with third parties.

SPECIAL PERMISSIONS THIS APP ASKS FOR, AND WHY

- Location (foreground and background): required by Android itself to return any cell signal information, and used to map network coverage along your routes.
- Usage Access: lets the app detect which app is in the foreground, for the purposes described above - not to monitor your activity for any other reason.
- Display over other apps: lets the occasional quality-rating prompt appear right away, so your answer stays close in time to the network conditions it's about, rather than needing you to remember to open the app later.
- Notifications: used only for a low-priority "collection active" status indicator and the quality-rating prompts.
- Battery optimization exemption: needed so the app can keep collecting reliably over the weeks-long study, since Android aggressively suspends background apps otherwise.

YOUR RIGHTS

Participation is voluntary. You can stop data collection at any time from the app's Status screen, or withdraw completely by uninstalling the app - either way, no further data will be collected from your device. To request that already-uploaded data tied to your device be deleted, contact bilalkouotou@gmail.com with your anonymous device ID from the Status screen.

QUESTIONS OR CONCERNS

This study is conducted by ENGR. KOUOTOU AHMAD BILAL, from the UNIVERSITY OF BUEA, under THE VICE CHANCELORS' approval. Contact bilalkouotou@gmail.com with any questions.

By tapping "I agree, continue" below, you confirm you've read this and voluntarily agree to participate.

Android requires location permission before it will return cell signal readings (RSRP, RSRQ, SINR) at all - this is a platform restriction, not something specific to this app. Approximate location is also used to map coverage along your usual routes for the drive-test portion of the study.\n\nWe also request phone-state access, needed on some Android versions to read full cell information.
Without this, signal telemetry and route mapping cannot be collected. You can grant it later from the app\'s Permissions screen.

Telemetry needs to be recorded while the app isn\'t open, so Android requires a separate \"Allow all the time\" location grant for background collection (on Android 11+ this may open a system Settings screen rather than a dialog - choose \"Allow all the time\" there).\n\nWe also ask for notification access, used only for the low-priority \"collection active\" status notification and the occasional one-tap quality rating prompt - never for ads or unrelated alerts.
Foreground location wasn\'t granted on the previous screen, so background location can\'t be requested yet.

To tag measurements with which app is active - specifically to detect a social-media or video-call session for quality labelling - the app needs Usage Access. This is a system-protected setting, so Android will take you to a Settings screen where you can find "QoESense" and turn it on.

We also ask you to exempt the app from battery optimization, since Android aggressively suspends background apps otherwise, which would create gaps of missing data over the weeks-long study.

Finally, "display over other apps" lets the occasional one-tap quality rating pop up right when it's relevant, over whatever app you're using at the time, instead of only showing as a notification you'd have to open yourself. It disappears on its own within a few seconds either way.
Display over other apps: not granted
The background service is sampling every ~60s (every ~15s during a video call) and buffering into Room. A Wi-Fi-only worker uploads batches to Cloud Storage roughly hourly.
Background collection is off. It normally starts automatically after onboarding - this toggle is mainly for testing.
